Associations in a genomic range

Source: R/range.R
og_range.Rd

Returns every Association of analyses between start and end on chromosome: positions are GRCh38, one-based and inclusive. The query runs as Jobs on the API, and og_range() waits for them (see vignette("large-queries-and-jobs")).

Usage

og_range(
  src,
  analyses,
  chromosome,
  start,
  end,
  observed_only = FALSE,
  original_units = FALSE,
  releases = NULL
)

Arguments

src

A Source, from og_api().

analyses

Analysis identifiers (see og_analyses()).

chromosome

One chromosome, such as "9" or "X".

start, end

The first and last position, inclusive.

observed_only

Leave out Imputed Associations.

original_units

Give beta and se in the trait's original units, as in og_tophits().

releases

Store Releases to use, as in og_analyses().

Value

A data frame with og_provenance() attached.

Details

One Job takes at most 10 Mb and 10 Analyses (from at most 10 GWAS Stores). A wider range or more Analyses is split into windows of at most 10 Mb, crossed with Analyses, run a few at a time (og_api(max_in_flight = )), and put back together: you get the rows an unsplit request would give, ordered by Analysis (in the order asked), chromosome, position and ALID, with every Job in og_provenance(). A range with more Associations than the API will return in one Job fails with opengwasr_request_too_large; it is never split to get round that. The columns are those of og_associations().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
src <- og_api()
og_range(src, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", chromosome = "9", start = 22090000, end = 22130000)
} # }
